response.title: what are the main differences between the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 and the BLUETTI AC200L
response.answer:
The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, and BLUETTI AC200L are all portable power stations using LiFePO₄ batteries, but they target somewhat different needs.

The biggest distinction is battery capacity versus portability:

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus: A versatile 1 kWh unit with fast charging, strong solar input, and UPS functionality.

BLUETTI Elite 200 V2: Roughly twice the battery capacity, with an emphasis on energy storage in a relatively compact package.

Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2: A lightweight, fast-charging 1 kWh option, particularly attractive for portability.

BLUETTI AC200L: A larger 2 kWh power station with higher continuous output and expandable battery capacity.

2. What the differences mean in practice
Shop

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus

Best for solar charging flexibility and small home backup setups. Its two independent 500W solar inputs are especially useful when using panels with different orientations. You can also add battery capacity later, rather than buying a larger station immediately.

Shop

BLUETTI Elite 200 V2

Best for getting approximately 2 kWh of storage and high appliance output in one unit. It offers the highest continuous wattage here and the highest advertised battery cycle life. The drawback is that its capacity cannot be expanded.

Shop

Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2

Best for camping, carrying around, and quick recharging. It is the lightest of the four and delivers 2,000W of AC output despite its small battery. Its main limitations are 600W solar input and no battery expansion.

Shop

BLUETTI AC200L

Best for more permanent backup systems, RVs, and larger solar setups. Its advantages include 1,200W solar input, support for higher-voltage solar arrays, expandable storage, and a 30A RV outlet. It is also the heaviest unit.
